mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a UNRATE decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it may indicate monetary tightening, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which could result in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 35% of the 20-day windows following a FEDFUNDS rate above 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in GDP (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong economic demand, which may boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following concurrent GDPC1 and HOUST growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over six months may signal supply chain constraints, leading to potential inflation and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following a 2% INDPRO increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real federal spending (RSAFS) indicates increased government demand, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 45% of the 5-day windows following an RSAFS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) may indicate a strong labor market, which could lead to wage inflation and potentially negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 35% of the 20-day windows following a PAYEMS growth above 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls, it may indicate conflicting monetary and labor market conditions, leading to increased market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following FEDFUNDS increases and UNRATE decreases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GDP (GDPC1) following a recession indicates economic recovery, which may boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 35% of the 60-day windows following a GDPC1 rebound, the hypothesis is rejected.
